title: I was looking for something in my room and wished I could tilt the whole floor and slide everything out of the way. So I made that a puzzle
author: office-canard
selftext:
I was looking for something in my room and wished I could just tilt the whole room and slide everything out of the way at once. That became TILT ROOM.



It started as a side view of a room you rotate 90 degrees at a time. Then I realized what I really wanted was for the player to choose which way to tip it first. So it became a 3D kid's room, and you tilt the floor with the arrow pad, or the arrow keys on PC.



Every toy slides at once. Your job is to get the round teddy bear out through the open door.



\- Shelves don't move. Blocks slide all the way.

\- Toy cars only move along one axis.

\- The wind-up train moves one square along its rail every time you tilt.

\- Rugs stop whatever slides onto them. Curves turn things 90 degrees.

\- If a block or a car slides into the doorway, it's blocked, and there's no undo.



The bear is a round, lifeless plush that tumbles around the room. When it reaches the door, it twitches, sits up, blinks, looks around, and walks out on its own. The music is a lullaby. It's a kid's room at night.



How AI fit in: Claude wrote all of the code, and all the toys are built in code. The 500 rooms are generated and then filtered hard. A room only survives if every toy in it has a job: take any one out and it can't be solved, turn a car into a block and it can't be solved, stop the train and it can't be solved. Random tilting has to fail almost every time. The rules, the toys, and the bear coming to life were my calls.
